title: Tiered alert routing and evidence automation
content:
Purpose:
This runbook defines how to route alerts by severity and ownership, automatically capture forensic-grade evidence from our RBAC v2-aware audit logs, and ensure SIEM exports contain the fields needed for fast triage and post‑incident analysis. It is intended for on-call security engineers, SREs supporting the security stack, and the incident commander during a security incident.

Scope:
- Applies to infrastructure and application alerts that originate from: Redwood audit logs, host instrumentation, network IDS, and third-party signals forwarded to our SIEM.
- Covers alert routing logic, required audit fields, automated evidence collection recipes, and handoff procedures to forensics and legal.
- Not a containment checklist; containment steps are in the containment playbook referenced in linked artifacts.

Key definitions and assumptions:
- RBAC v2 context: users are mapped to numeric "role_id" and logical role names (e.g., platform-admin, infra-operator, app-readonly). Role changes are logged as role_change events in audit logs with before/after role_id and performed_by.
- Evidence grade: we aim to collect tamper-evident artifacts (signed/hashed exports) and preserve chain-of-custody metadata (who, when, retention policy).

Alert categorization and routing (summary):
- P1 (Critical): Active data exfiltration, keys compromised, privilege escalation to platform-admin, or core control-plane lateral movement. Route: paging to Security Pager (oncall sec-pager), notify SRE lead, auto-create incident in Jira SEC-INC.
- P2 (High): Suspicious role_change, repeated failed auths from unusual IPs to admin endpoints, abnormal export/backup requests. Route: Security Slack #sec-alerts, SRE on-call, log to SIEM with evidence bundle.
- P3 (Medium): Non-blocking anomalies (e.g., rare API errors, single failed role_change). Route: security triage queue (async).

Routing rules (implementation notes):
- All alerts must include: alert_id, timestamp_utc, source, rule_id, severity_hint, correlated_entities (user_id, session_id, host), and earliest_event_id.
- For RBAC-sensitive alerts (role_change, impersonation, policy-mod), add: role_before, role_after, performed_by_role_id, performed_by_user_email.
- Use the routing engine (alert-router service) to match rule_id -> channel. If rule_id starts with rbac.v2.*, force include the rbac tag and route to #rbac-review channel and P2+ escalation.

Audit log schema required fields (recommended minimal schema for SIEM ingestion):
- event_id (string)
- event_type (string) e.g. role_change, auth_failure, token_issue, svc_account_action
- timestamp (ISO8601)
- tenant_id (string)
- user_id (string)
- user_email (string)
- actor_role_id (string)
- actor_role_name (string)
- target_user_id (string) optional
- target_role_before (string)
- target_role_after (string)
- source_ip (string)
- user_agent (string)
- request_id (string)
- trace_id (string) optional but preferred
- raw_payload (string) base64 of original event for replay
- event_hash (sha256) of canonicalized event for tamper detection
- signed_by (string) service that signed the export

SIEM export and index mapping (practical guidance):
- Index pattern: sec-audit-YYYY.MM.dd (daily) with alias sec-audit-current for dashboards.
- Use event_type, actor_role_name, and tenant_id as primary aggregators.
- Create SIEM rule examples:
  - rule: role_change_to_platform_admin -> condition: event_type:role_change AND target_role_after:platform-admin AND source_ip not in corp_vpn_ranges -> trigger P1.
  - rule: elevated_token_issuance -> condition: token_issue AND actor_role_name in [infra-operator] AND requested_scopes include admin -> trigger P2.
- Store raw_payload as an immutable field; do not populate searchable text fields with full payload to limit noise and PII exposure.

Automated evidence collection recipes (safe, reproducible):
1) Role change alert automation (RBAC v2):
   - Trigger: alert-router sends webhook to evidence-collector when rule_id == rbac.v2.role_change AND severity >= P2.
   - Collector tasks (ordered):
     a) query auditstore for event_id and +/- 5m window using request_id and trace_id; export matching events as ndjson.
     b) snapshot policy state (current role mappings table) from config service: GET /api/v1/rbac/roles?version=latest -> store JSON and compute sha256.
     c) collect related cloud provider audit entries (if any) using cloud-audit-linking service with tenant_id + trace_id.
     d) capture ephemeral host process list and network sockets for any hosts in correlated_entities via ssm-run-command.
     e) package artifacts into evidence bundle, sign with evidence-key (HSM-backed) and push to secure-bucket with path: evidence/{incident_id}/{bundle_id}.tgz.sig
   - Outputs: signed_bundle_url, bundle_hash, collection_timestamps, collector_run_id. Attach these to the SIEM event via enrichment API.

2) Suspicious export/backup request:
   - Trigger: export patterns matched OR large data transfer to external IP.
   - Collector: snapshot export job metadata, access logs for object store, temporary presigned-URL audit, and user session logs. Hash and sign.

Chain-of-custody and retention notes:
- Every evidence bundle must include metadata fields: collected_by, collector_version, host_hashes, and evidence_hash. Store these fields in SIEM as evidence_* tags for search.
- Short-term retention for active incidents: 90 days with immediate access. Compliance retention: move signed bundles to cold storage with retention 7 years (triggered by legal hold tag).

Quick triage checklist (on-call):
- Step 0: Read alert summary and check severity hint. Confirm alert_id and timestamp.
- Step 1: Expand correlated_entities: who is affected and what roles changed?
- Step 2: Query SIEM: event_id and trace_id. Pull attached evidence bundle URL if present.
- Step 3: Confirm whether role_change was via UI or infra API (look at request_id and actor_role_name).
- Step 4: If actor_role is platform-admin or change happened outside corp IPs -> escalate to P1 immediately.
- Step 5: Kick off automated evidence collector if not already run (manual trigger endpoint: POST /ops/evidence/collect with alert_id).
- Step 6: Create incident ticket if P1/P2 and notify legal and CCR leads.
- Step 7: Preserve snapshot and avoid remediation that would destroy artifacts until forensics sign-off.

Escalation matrix (internal contacts):
- security-pager (primary): oncall-sec (rotating)
- security-lead: Asha Patel (pager backup)
- infra-sre-oncall: Riley Chen
- platform-admin-owner: Mateo Alvarez
- legal-notify: legal-oncall@redwood.com

Playbook snippets: useful CLI commands and endpoints
- Pull raw audit events: curl -H "X-Service-Key: $KEY" "https://audit.redwood.internal/v1/events?event_id={event_id}&window=10m"
- Trigger collector: curl -X POST -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"alert_id":"ALERT123"}' https://ops.redwood.internal/evidence/collect
- Verify bundle hash: aws s3 cp s3://evidence-buckets/{path} - | sha256sum -c -

Post-incident and postmortem pointers:
- When incident moves to "resolved", attach the evidence bundle IDs and signer_info to the Jira SEC-INC ticket and add a short summary of collection timeline.
- Use the postmortem template: confluence:SEC-POSTMORTEM-TEMPLATE and fill sections: timeline, detection-factors, evidence-collection-timeline, missed-assertions (e.g., missing fields in audit logs), and recommended actions.

Common failure modes and mitigations (lessons learned):
- Missing trace_id in events: we now recommend always including trace_id at service boundary; mitigation: when absent, fall back to request_id plus time-window fuzzy search. Add a Jira ticket to instrument missing sources.
- Evidence collector times out on large windows: set collector default window to 30m and escalate for manual wide-window exports. Implement streaming export for high-volume incidents.
- Role IDs mismatched between services: run nightly reconciliation job; during triage, use role mapping service to canonicalize ids.

Action items (short-term):
- [ ] Add actor_role_name to every auth event across app services (owner: eng-platform, jira:SEC-5421).
- [ ] Add event_hash generation in audit pipeline and surface it in SIEM (owner: infra-logging).
- [ ] Create automated test that triggers role_change alert and validates evidence collector end-to-end (owner: applied-ml security infra).

Notes and context (freeform):
- This document is intentionally procedural and focused on automation and observability; it does not replace the containment or legal hold procedures but complements them by ensuring we capture usable evidence quickly.
- We should iterate on the SIEM rule examples above as we see false positives; tagging and enrichment reduce analyst time.
